KSHV is a leading cause of infection-related cancers in sub-Saharan Africa and immunocompromised individuals worldwide. Therefore, it is vital to identify the underlying mechanisms of viral infection and transmission to effectively identify specific therapeutic strategies and combat the disease.

AbstractSince the spring of 2023, the Kuroshio Extension had shifted northward, leading to a marine heat wave (MHW) immediately to the east of northern Japan. Although several previous studies have investigated the impact of MHWs on weather on land during the warm season, only a few studies have investigated their impact during wintertime. This study focused on a heavy rainfall event along the eastern coast of northern Japan on January 21, 2024.

AbstractFocus groups with 54 participants, mostly native Spanish speakers and members of economically disadvantaged communities in Miami-Dade County, were conducted to evaluate the National Hurricane Center's Track Forecast Cone. Responses were examined using Kosslyn's analytic scheme as a diagnostic framework for identifying design issues at the syntactic, semantic, and pragmatic levels. Findings confirm previously documented misinterpretations, such as users perceiving the cone as a storm boundary or as indicating storm growth over time.
